title: LA-ICP-MS Geochronology TAPP (geochronTAPP)
description: Laser-ablation ICP-MS geochronology (U-Pb / Pb-Pb and related) Technique-Aligned Protocol Profile. Covers LA-Q/SF/MC-ICP-MS variants. Generated from docs/LA-ICPMS_Geochron_Horstwood_TAPP_v6.xlsx via the path-driven pipeline.

@context.description: JSON-LD context declaring the namespace prefixes used in a method definition. Required for the document to be a valid JSON-LD instance. Bound prefixes must include schema (always), cdi (DDI-CDI), and ada (ADA vocabulary). Additional prefixes (bios, dqv, prov, skos) are recommended when those vocabularies are used in the body of the definition.

@id.description: Persistent URI for this TAPP definition in the registry.

@type.description: Must include prov:Plan, cdi:Activity, schema:Action, ada:TAPPDefinition, and bios:LabProtocol. The TAPP is a PLAN (prov:Plan / bios:LabProtocol) — a reusable procedure description that prescribes the analysis, NOT the analysis occurrence (that is the prov:Activity in adaProduct.prov:wasGeneratedBy, which references this plan via prov:used). As a plan, its instrument / bios:computationalTool / bios:reagent are directly-specified resources (bios:LabProtocol convention), not prov:used entities.

A schema:GeoShape bounding box. The geometry is described with a set of latitude/longitude pairs (in that order).The documentation for schema:GeoShape states 'Either whitespace or commas can be used to separate latitude and longitude; whitespace should be used when writing a list of several such points.'

schema:box.description: A GeoShape box defines an area on the surface of the earth defined by point locations of the southwest corner and northeast corner of the rectangle in latitude-longitude coordinates. A space should be used to separate the latitude and longitude values. The two corner coordinate points are separated by a space. 'East longitude' means positive longitude values are east of the prime (Greenwich) meridian.

anyOf.description: A schema:GeoShape curvilinear trace, for resource related to a linear trace like a ship track or airplane flight line

schema:line.description: A GeoShape box defines a curvilinear geometry as a string of latitude-longitude coordinates. A space should be used to separate the latitude and longitude values. The coordinate point pairs are also separated by a space. 'East longitude' means positive longitude values are east of the prime (Greenwich) meridian. e.g. '39.33 120.77 40.44 123.96 41.00 121.34'

NOTE that the location specified here should be the same as the schema.org point or contained within the specified bounding box.

schema:actionProcess.description: The standard workflow for this method, expressed as a schema:HowTo containing an ordered sequence of workflow steps. Each step is a cdi:Activity + schema:Action describing a distinct phase (sample preparation, calibration, acquisition, data processing, quality control). Steps carry their own parameters, reagents, instruments, and sub-steps.

schema:additionalProperty.description: Method-level Advanced-protocol parameters that apply across all workflow steps. Editable parameters are schema:PropertyValueSpecification entries (a default the analyst may override); read-only parameters are schema:PropertyValue entries carrying the fixed protocol value. Replaces the former ada:methodParameters. Technique TAPP profiles constrain the allowed entries via $refs to the parameterTemplates (specifications) and parameterValues (values) registries. Step-specific parameters should be placed on the appropriate workflow step instead.

anyOf.description: A parameter specification for the method, typed as schema:PropertyValueSpecification. Uses schema.org properties for value constraints (defaultValue, minValue, maxValue, readonlyValue, valueRequired) and ada: extensions for analytical method semantics (fieldScope, category, tier). Link to a controlled vocabulary via schema:inDefinedTermSet.

schema:propertyID.description: URI identifying this parameter type in a formal vocabulary. Links to a skos:Concept or similar term definition. URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}).

schema:inDefinedTermSet.description:
Controlled vocabulary providing allowed values for this parameter. When present, form renders a dropdown/select populated from the vocabulary. Four shapes are accepted: (1) a plain URI string identifying an external SKOS ConceptScheme; (2) an object reference ({"@id": "<uri>"}) to a vocabulary defined elsewhere; (3) a LabeledLink (LinkRole with name and URL); (4) an inline schema:DefinedTermSet enumerating the allowed values
    as schema:DefinedTerm objects (replaces the prior ada:enumeration).

Inline schema:DefinedTermSet listing the allowed values as schema:DefinedTerm objects. Use when no external vocabulary URI is available; replaces the deprecated ada:enumeration property.

schema:defaultValue.description: The default value for this parameter. For constant parameters (readonlyValue=true), this is the fixed value. For editable parameters, this is the pre-filled default.

anyOf.title: Imaging
anyOf.description: Pre-ablation characterisation imaging (typically cathodoluminescence [CL] or backscattered electron [BSE]) used to reveal internal zoning, inherited cores, and metamict domains for selecting valid spot locations, including the imaging instrument and settings used.

anyOf.title: Faraday Cup Array Configuration
anyOf.description: Description of the multi-collector Faraday cup array: total number of Faraday cup detectors (fixed and moveable), their labelled positions, and the presence and position of any ion counter (SEM) or Daly detector. The number and span of cups constrains which isotope combinations can be simultaneously collected.

anyOf.title: Faraday Cup Amplifier Resistor Values
anyOf.description: Resistance values (Ω) of the feedback resistors in the Faraday cup amplifiers. Standard amplifiers use 10¹¹ Ω resistors; high-gain amplifiers (10¹² or 10¹³ Ω) are fitted to selected cups to improve signal-to-noise for very low-intensity beams (e.g., low-abundance Pb isotopes in young or low-U material).

anyOf.title: Faraday Cup Gain Calibration Method
anyOf.description: Method used to calibrate the relative gain (amplification factor) of each Faraday cup amplifier at the start of or during each analytical session. Relative gain differences between amplifiers cause systematic errors in isotope ratios if uncorrected. For instruments with ion-counting detectors, also describes the SEM-to-Faraday cross-calibration sequence.

anyOf.title: Ablation Pit Depth/Ablation Rate
anyOf.description: Depth of the ablation pit produced under the registered laser conditions, the method used to measure it, and the resulting per-pulse ablation rate. Characterises the achievable depth/time resolution of the procedure.

anyOf.title: Make-up Gas Flow (L min⁻¹)
anyOf.description: Source and estimated flow rate of any make-up gas added downstream of the ablation cell, including any desolvating nebuliser used for tracer co-aspiration.

anyOf.title: Collector Configuration
anyOf.description: Assignment of isotope masses to Faraday cup or ion counter detector positions for this procedure. For static multi-collection, one configuration applies throughout the measurement; for multi-dynamic procedures, lists all configurations and the cycling sequence. Includes interference-monitor masses collected alongside analyte isotopes.

anyOf.title: Number of Blocks per Measurement
anyOf.description: Number of measurement blocks acquired per spot. Each block typically begins with a baseline (on-peak zero) measurement before the analytical cycles. Multiple blocks allow inspection of signal stability and within-measurement drift.

anyOf.title: Number of Cycles per Block
anyOf.description: Number of measurement cycles acquired per block. One cycle corresponds to a single set of simultaneous Faraday cup readings integrated for the duration in Integration Time per Cycle.

anyOf.title: Integration Time per Cycle
anyOf.description: Duration of signal integration per measurement cycle. Total integration time per spot = (Number of Cycles per Block) × (Integration Time per Cycle) × (Number of Blocks per Measurement).

anyOf.title: IC Dead Time (ns)
anyOf.description: Dead time of each ion-counting detector channel, used in dead-time correction of high count rates.

anyOf.title: Signal Smoothing
anyOf.description: Description of any signal smoothing device or approach installed between the ablation cell and the ICP-MS to reduce pulse-to-pulse signal variability.

anyOf.title: ICP Tuning
anyOf.description: Description of the approach used to optimise ICP plasma conditions prior to analysis, including the reference material used for tuning and the acceptance criteria.

anyOf.title: Doubly-Charged Species Monitor
anyOf.description: The mass ratio monitored to estimate doubly-charged ion (M²⁺) formation during instrument tuning.

anyOf.title: Doubly-Charged Species Production
anyOf.description: Measured percentage of doubly-charged ion production for the monitored species at the time of instrument tuning.

anyOf.title: Instrument Warm-up / Session Duration Limit
anyOf.description: Minimum warm-up time required after plasma ignition before analyses begin, and any maximum session duration enforced to maintain stable operating conditions.

anyOf.title: Baseline Measurement Approach
anyOf.description: Method and timing for measuring the ion beam baseline (background) during acquisition, distinct from the data-processing-level blank subtraction method (see Gas Blank, Group 5). For LA-ICP-MS, baseline is measured with the laser off (gas blank), typically before each ablation or block.

anyOf.title: Multi-Run Sequential Analysis Design
anyOf.description: Whether the procedure uses a single acquisition pass or multiple sequential runs on the same sample location, each optimised for different analytical objectives.

anyOf.title: E-scan Range
anyOf.description: Electric scan range used for peak acquisition, expressed as percentage of the centre mass. Varies the accelerating voltage to cover nearby masses without re-scanning the magnet. Applicable only to sector-field instruments.

anyOf.title: Triple Scanning Mode
anyOf.description: Whether each mass peak is scanned three times per cycle and the results averaged, to reduce noise from short-term magnetic field instabilities. Applicable only to sector-field instruments with this capability.

anyOf.title: Other Information
anyOf.description: Supplementary methodological context not captured by the structured fields above, as reported in Table 3 of Horstwood et al. (2016) — in the source paper's own example, notes on ablation-cell and sample-line configuration for depth-profiling/single-pulse ablation studies, a variant not otherwise in scope for this single-mode (Spot Analysis) TAPP.

anyOf.title: Mass Fractionation Law
anyOf.description: Mathematical law used to parameterize instrumental isotope mass fractionation as a function of mass difference. Not stated in Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) for the worked example; the exponential law is most widely used and theoretically best justified for MC-ICP-MS.

anyOf.title: Uncertainty Level and Propagation
anyOf.description: Uncertainty level at which ages/ratios are quoted (e.g., 1σ, 2σ) and the method used to propagate component uncertainties (e.g., quadratic addition) into the final reported value.

anyOf.title: Matrix Offset Correction (LIEF)
anyOf.description: Whether an empirical correction was applied to account for systematic differences in laser-induced elemental fractionation (LIEF) patterns between the external calibration standard and the sample matrix.

anyOf.title: Spike / Outlier Filtering Approach
anyOf.description: Method used to identify and remove anomalous signal spikes arising from micronuggets, inclusions, cracks, or instrument artifacts during time-resolved signal processing.

anyOf.title: Double-Spike Isotope Pair
anyOf.description: The pair of enriched isotopes used to construct a double spike for combined mass bias and/or common-Pb correction. Both isotopes must be naturally rare and free from isobaric interferences. Record 'N/A' if double-spike method is not used.

anyOf.title: Double-Spike Mixing Ratio
anyOf.description: Target proportion of double-spike signal relative to total analyte signal in the spiked mixture. An optimal mixing ratio minimises error propagation through the double-spike inversion. Record 'N/A' if double-spike method is not used.

anyOf.title: Double-Spike Inversion Algorithm
anyOf.description: Mathematical algorithm used to simultaneously solve for the true sample isotope ratio and the mass fractionation factor from the measured spike-sample mixture. Record 'N/A' if double-spike method is not used.

anyOf.title: Memory Effect Mitigation
anyOf.description: Procedure applied to identify and minimise memory effects from high-concentration elements in the previous sample or standard that may contaminate subsequent analyses.

anyOf.title: Normalization/Standards-Based Correction
anyOf.description: Any post-acquisition normalization applied to correct for systematic biases identified from secondary reference materials.

ada:sampleIntroduction.description: Configuration by which the ablated aerosol is delivered to the plasma, including any co-aspirated tracer or spike solution (e.g., a Tl solution used for instrumental mass bias correction, or a ²³⁵U spike used for isotope dilution).

items.description: Procedure-level declaration of the analytical mode(s) this procedure covers. This TAPP is scoped to static spot ablation only, consistent with Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016). No mode-flag columns are used in this TAPP because only one mode is in scope.

ada:ablationSamplingMode.description: Sampling mode or ablation pattern used during analysis, as described in Table 3 of Horstwood et al. (2016).

ada:spotDiameter.description: Diameter of the laser spot as set in the acquisition method (nominal/target value).

ada:ablationSpotDuration.description: Total on-sample ablation time per spot, as set in the acquisition method.

ada:carrierGasFlowRate.description: Identity and plumbing configuration of the gas used to transport the ablated aerosol from the cell to the torch, including the procedure-registered flow rate(s).

ada:rfPower.description: ICP radiofrequency forward power. Session-tunable within procedure-defined bounds during plasma optimisation; consistent with the analogous, tunable treatment of RF Power across LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS and all three solution ICP-MS TAPPs.

ada:coolantGasFlowRate.description: Flow rate of the outer (coolant/plasma) argon gas stream that sustains the ICP plasma. Determines plasma volume and stability.

ada:auxiliaryGasFlowRate.description: Flow rate of the intermediate (auxiliary) argon gas stream that positions the plasma relative to the load coil. Affects ion extraction efficiency and oxide production rates.

ada:plasmaThermalMode.description: Whether the ICP plasma is operated under cool plasma or normal (hot) plasma conditions. Normal plasma is standard for U-(Th-)Pb geochronology; cool plasma would reduce sensitivity for these high-mass analytes and is not typically used.

ada:massesMeasured.description: Mass-to-charge positions (isotope masses) this procedure is designed to measure. Defines the scope of the procedure; the analyst may record the specific subset actually measured in a given session.

ada:reportedVariablesAndUnits.description: The final reported chemical/isotopic variable(s) and their units — distinct from Masses Measured, which records raw acquisition scope. Covers isotope ratios (both common-Pb corrected and uncorrected, where applicable), elemental/isotopic concentrations, and any derived quantities (age, δ or ε notation) with their reference standard where relevant. For non-mass-spectrometry techniques, this field is generalised to any reported physical or chemical property and its units.

ada:integrationTimePerPeakDwellTimesQuad.description: Count time (dwell time) per mass position for each measured isotope, and the settling time allowed between mass jumps, as reported in Table 3 of Horstwood et al. (2016). Applies to sequential (Q/SF) mass-hopping acquisition; for simultaneous multi-collector acquisition see Number of Blocks per Measurement, Number of Cycles per Block, and Integration Time per Cycle.

ada:totalIntegrationTimePerOutputDataPoi.description: Total duty-cycle time for one complete mass-scan sweep (sum of all per-isotope dwell times and settling times), which sets the time resolution of the down-hole signal. Applies to sequential (Q/SF) acquisition.

ada:oxideProductionMethodAndThreshold.description: Method used to quantify plasma oxide production and the acceptance threshold applied before commencing analysis. ThO⁺/Th⁺ (mass 248/232) is the standard proxy for U-Th-Pb geochronology, directly relevant to Th/U ratio accuracy.

ada:analysisSequence.description: Repeating order of primary calibration standard(s), quality control standard(s), and unknown analyses within a measurement session.

ada:signalCollectionMode.description: Mode used to collect ion signal across the monitored masses. In peak hopping mode, the quadrupole jumps sequentially between pre-set mass positions and dwells at each peak. Applicable only to quadrupole-based instruments; this concept does not extend to collision-cell-equipped multi-collector instruments (e.g., Nu Sapphire, Thermo Neoma MS/MS), whose collector array performs genuinely simultaneous multi-collection regardless of whether a collision/reaction cell is present upstream. Some such instruments (e.g., Neoma MS/MS) instead use a pre-cell mass filter of a fundamentally different, non-quadrupole design to pre-select a mass window before the cell — a distinct concept not currently captured by any field in this TAPP.

items.description: Mass resolution mode assigned to each analyte in this procedure. The selected resolution determines which polyatomic interferences (e.g., ¹⁸⁶W¹⁶O⁺ on ²⁰²Hg, relevant to common-Pb correction) are physically resolved by the magnetic sector. Applicable only to sector-field instruments.

ada:gasBlank.description: Duration of the background (gas blank) measurement and how it is applied to correct the ablation signal.

items.description: Method used to correct for laser-induced elemental fractionation (LIEF), including any assumption about reference-material/sample behaviour equivalence, as reported in Table 3 of Horstwood et al. (2016).

ada:massBiasCorrectionStrategy.description: Primary strategy used to correct for instrumental isotopic mass fractionation (mass bias/mass discrimination).

ada:internalNormalizationElementAndIsoto.description: Element and isotope ratio used as the internal normalization standard for mass bias correction, and how the resulting correction is applied to analyte ratios.

ada:commonPbCorrectionCompositionAndUnce.description: Whether a common-Pb correction was applied, and if so, the model composition (e.g., Stacey and Kramers 1975) and its uncertainty used in the correction.

ada:constantsAndReferenceValuesUsed.description: Physical constants and reference values used in data reduction to calculate the final reported quantity (e.g., decay constants for age calculation, the 238U/235U ratio used to convert measured 235U-based data to 207Pb/235U, or other citable reference values), together with their source. Distinct from Reference Material Information (Group 6), which documents accepted values for specific calibration/validation materials rather than universal physical constants. Critical for traceability: community-recommended values for decay constants and isotope ratios are periodically revised (e.g., the 238U/235U ratio revision by Hiess et al. 2012), and a reported age or ratio can only be correctly reinterpreted against a future revision if the constants originally used are known.

items.description: Documents cases where different analytes are calibrated using different strategies within the same session. If a single strategy applies uniformly, record that here.
enum: Single strategy: matrix-matched primary reference material for all analytes

ada:signalIntegrationIntervalMethod.description: Approach used to select the stable signal interval for integration during data reduction, and to exclude anomalous signals from inclusions, cracks, or mixed domains. Central to interpreting excess scatter/MSWD in the resulting age population.

items.description: Whether isobaric interference corrections were applied for any measured isotope in this procedure. A procedure-level Boolean; element-specific detail is in Interfering Species and Interference Correction Method.
Elemental or molecular species overlapping with the measured isotope, relevant to U-Th-Pb geochronology (e.g., ²⁰⁴Hg on ²⁰⁴Pb, relevant to the Common-Pb Correction field above).
Equation or procedure used to correct for isobaric interferences, including the reference material or monitor isotope used to characterise it.

ada:isotopeDilutionDataReductionMethod.description: Mass balance approach used to calculate sample mass fractions from spike-sample isotope ratio measurements, relevant when a concentration spike (e.g., ²³⁵U, as in Table 3's own worked example) is co-aspirated. Record 'None' if isotope dilution is not used.

ada:primaryStandardName.description: Primary reference material used to calibrate the instrument and convert raw signal intensities to ages/isotope ratios. Include citation for the accepted values used.

items.description: Quality-control reference material(s) analysed as unknowns alongside samples in the same session to assess accuracy and monitor drift. Include citation/accepted values for each.

ada:calibrationMeasurementFrequency.description: How often the primary calibration standard is measured relative to unknown samples within a session, i.e. the bracketing interval used to monitor and correct for instrumental drift. Implied but not stated explicitly in Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) via the validation-material n counts.

schema:name.description: Human-readable name for this instrument.

schema:description.description: Text description of this instrument, its purpose, and capabilities.

schema:alternateName.description: Alternate name(s), e.g. specific make/model designation, common abbreviation.

schema:category.description: Instrument type classification(s) from a controlled vocabulary.
